brief: Zero Hedge's Oct 2 wrap: oil, stocks, bonds, the dollar, gold and bitcoin all rose while European sovereign bonds sold off. Brent topped $100 on rebuilt Iran-war premium (Rubio expelling Iran's UN delegation, a Pentagon carrier group and 9,000-10,000 troops headed to the region, Trump calling renewed Iran bombing 'possible' post-midterms) plus physical tightness (record premiums at the biggest US storage hub, Dated Brent above futures); Capital Economics says low inventories put a floor under price. Diesel is separately strained by Gulf turmoil and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, with the US threatening France and Germany with an export ban unless they release emergency diesel reserves. Thursday's European bond selloff (French OATs and CDS, Italian BTPs vs Bunds) drove a US Treasury safe-haven bid that, combined with a dovish Jefferson comment outweighing four hawkish Fed officials, pulled 10-year yields off a 24-year high even as oil and a top-quintile ISM prices-paid print argued the other way. Stocks chopped, with the Mag7 flat and underperforming the S&P 493; Micron rallied on an upbeat AI-capex quarter despite a margin warning. BTIG's Krinsky calls yields tactically exhausted and flags low options hedging as raising October volatility risk despite the month's seasonally bullish history.
